newsitem.title: USA: Bentsen - would prefer dlr not rise further - RFTV.
newsitem.headline: Bentsen - would prefer dlr not rise further - RFTV.

text.p: Former U.S. Treasury Secretary Lloyd Bentsen on Friday said the dollar is now trading at a "comfortable" level but he would rather not see it climb much further.
"I think we're at a comfortable level," Bentsen told Reuters Financial Television. "This is a strong dollar."

"If it continues to rise and goes substantially above this, of course, it puts us at a competitive disadvantage," Bentsen said, referring to the dollar's level against the yen. "I would prefer not to see it increase in value," he added.

Bentsen served as Treasury Secretary under President Clinton during the first two years of his administration. During his tenure, some currency traders believed Bentsen favored an informal ceiling on the dollar of around 113 yen.
In contrast to Bentsen's remarks, the current Treasury chief, Robert Rubin, has repeatedly touted the administration's support for a strong dollar.
At around 1150 EST/1650 GMT, the dollar stood at 113.15/25 yen, down from its opening in the U.S. at 113.67/70 yen.
